title: Trion Hall effect in electron-hole double layers
authors: Raghav Chaturvedi, Phuong X. Nguyen, Patrick Knüppel, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan
abstract: The realization of Coulomb coupled electron-hole double layers in 2D semiconductor heterostructures has enabled the thermodynamic and transport studies of equilibrium exciton fluids without a magnetic field. By doping the exciton fluid with additional electrons/holes, an equilibrium fluid of trions - three particle bound states of electrons and holes - further emerge, providing the platform to explore new transport phenomena associated with such composite particles. Here we report the observation of a Hall effect for trions in MoSe2/WSe2 heterobilayers, which support Coulomb-coupled electron and hole fluids with tunable densities. The Hall effect arises from a Lorentz force on trions under a perpendicular magnetic field. It is manifested in both Hall drag measurements and standard Hall effect measurements on just one of the semiconductor layers. For negatively charged trions, an electron Hall effect is observed even in a hole doped WSe2 monolayer due to the presence of trion drags. The trion Hall effect also disappears when the trions are ionized at elevated temperatures and/or high trion densities. Our work opens the door for realizing quantum oscillations and the quantum Hall effect for trions.
summary: The study reports the observation of a measurable Hall effect for trions—three-particle bound states—in MoSe2/WSe2 heterobilayers. By measuring transport properties under magnetic fields, the authors confirm that these composite particles carry unique charge responses, including an electron-Hall effect in a hole layer. This opens avenues for studying quantum phenomena associated with multi-body correlated phases.
main_problem: The study aims to observe and characterize the Hall effect for trions (three-particle bound states of electrons and holes) in electron-hole double layers.
main_result: A distinct Trion Hall effect is observed, including an electron-Hall effect measured within a hole-doped layer due to negative trion drags. This confirms the existence and transport properties of these composite particles.
method: The research combines electrical transport measurements (standard Hall bar and Coulomb drag) with optical spectroscopy (reflection contrast) under perpendicular magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Coulomb-coupled electron-hole double layer realized in 2D semiconductor heterostructures, specifically MoSe2/WSe2 heterobilayers. The physics involves the formation and transport of excitons and trions within this coupled quantum well structure.

important_parameters: Temperature ($T \approx 1.5	ext{K}$ to $10	ext{K}$), Magnetic Field ($B$ up to $12	ext{T}$), Gate Voltages ($V_g$, $V_+$), and carrier densities.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed transport phenomena are dominated by the contributions of free carriers, excitons, and trions, which can be modeled using conductivity tensors.
figures_summary: Figures detail phase diagrams mapping out regions hosting different charge states (exciton insulator vs. trion fluid) as a function of magnetic field and gate voltage, alongside measurements showing the disappearance of the effect at high T or B.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence by first establishing the platform, then measuring transport coefficients ($R_{xx}, R_{xy}$, drag), mapping out phase boundaries in $B$-field/gate-voltage space, and finally confirming the physical mechanism through temperature and density dependence studies.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental realization of correlated electron physics beyond simple excitons, exploring three-body bound states (trions) and their unique magneto-transport signatures, which is highly relevant to strongly correlated materials research.
